The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following statements are true? 

- $f(x)$ is defined at $x=-1$
- ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)$ exists
- $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1$
feedback.worked_solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is true. The function $f(x)$ is defined at $x=-1$ and we have $f(-1)=1.$

- Statement II is false. We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x) & =2, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, both left-hand side and right-hand side limits exist but they are not the same. Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x)$ does not exist.

- Statement III is false. The function contains a break exactly at $x=-1$ and it's impossible to draw its graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.
